Name: Ayomán (Jahn 1910)
Remark: Taken down by Alfredo Jahn from Carmen Ramos (c. 83 years old) at San Miguel, Estado Lara, August 1910, in Jahn's 'alfabeto combinado, fonético' (see README). Also forms printed only in the Ayomán columns of the Jirajara and Gayón comparison tables.

Name: Ayomán (Oramas 1916, as quoted by Jahn)
Remark: Forms marked (O) in Jahn's Ayomán vocabulary: Luis R. Oramas, Materiales para el estudio de los dialectos Ayamán, Gayón, Jirajara, Ajagua (Caracas 1916); Oramas combined his own 1916 notes from Distrito Urdaneta with Párraga's earlier vocabularies. Spanish-based spelling.

Name: Ayamán vocabulary of Freitez Pineda 1907 (as quoted by Jahn)
Remark: Forms marked (F): Freitez Pineda's 'Vocabulario Ayamán' (Barquisimeto 1907), which Jahn (pp. 6-7, 261-262) shows mixes Jirajara words of Siquisique (Párraga) with Ayomán words of San Miguel; hence only the language-level Glottocode.

Name: Jirajara (Siquisique)
Remark: Jirajara column of Jahn's 'Vocabulario Jirajara de Siquisique (Estado Lara) comparado con el Ayomán'; Jahn (pp. 261-262) traces the Siquisique words to General Octaviano Párraga's list of c. 1880 (published by J. T. Pérez, 1886). Spanish-based spelling as printed by Jahn.

Name: Gayón (Jahn 1910)
Remark: Taken down by Alfredo Jahn in 1910 from Antolino Dobobuto, an old man of El Docoré (jurisdiction of Bobare, Estado Lara) (p. 273).

Name: Timote (Urrecheaga 1875-78; Jahn 1910)
Remark: Vocabulary ordered by Jahn from the manuscript of bachiller R. M. Urrecheaga, recorded 1875-78 among the Timotes of Timotes and the Mesa de Esnujaque (Trujillo/Mérida), expanded with Jahn's own 1910 notes from two old speakers at the Mesa de Esnujaque; Urrecheaga's spelling throughout. Jahn does not mark which words are his own. Fonseca's 'dialecto Cuicas' (1911) is the same Urrecheaga material (Jahn p. 326).
